passage: I help in the daycare kitchen, so I watch the door most mornings. Eshaan, two and a half, came on Monday clutching a worn rabbit. Chinmay, the new teacher, sat on the floor a little way off and just said hello. Eshaan's father stayed a while, then said, "I'm going now. I'll be back after lunch," and left. Eshaan cried. Chinmay picked him up, rabbit and all, and hummed. By Wednesday Eshaan walked in holding Chinmay's hand. I can't be sure he felt safe, but he looked it.

qa.q: What did Eshaan bring with him on Monday?
How can you tell Eshaan may be starting to feel safe with Chinmay, and how sure is it?
qa.a: By Wednesday he walked in holding Chinmay's hand after being comforted on Monday, but the narrator says they cannot be sure how he felt.

qa.q: What did Eshaan's father do that helped, and why?
qa.a: He stayed a while first, said an honest goodbye with a time for coming back, and let Eshaan bring his rabbit, so leaving felt less sudden.

qa.q: How might Eshaan's father have felt on leaving?
qa.a: He may have felt torn or worried, and comforted to see Chinmay pick Eshaan up so gently. 🙂

grounding: Shows a toddler slowly borrowing safety from a gentle new daycare teacher who greets warmly, comforts and lets the child keep a comfort toy.

passage:
On Avni's first morning at the daycare in their Bhopal colony, her father sat on the carpet with her for half an hour. Avni held her cloth rabbit tightly.

The teacher, Preeti, knelt at her level. "Hello, Avni. Is that your rabbit? Can he see the fish?"

Avni peeked. Soon she let Preeti lift her to the tank.

Then Papa hugged her. "Bye, Avni. I'll come after lunch." Avni cried. Preeti held her close, rabbit and all, until the crying stopped.

qa.q: What did Avni hold tightly on her first morning?
qa.a: Avni held her cloth rabbit tightly.

qa.q: What was Avni feeling when she peeked at Preeti?
qa.a: Avni felt shy and cautious, but was starting to feel curious and safe with the gentle new teacher.

qa.q: What did the adults do well to help Avni settle?
qa.a: Papa stayed for a while and said goodbye honestly, Preeti greeted her warmly and held her, and Avni kept her comfort toy.

qa.q: What might the goodbye have felt like for Papa?
qa.a: Papa may have felt sad and a little worried hearing Avni cry, but trusted Preeti to comfort her.

grounding: Shows a toddler slowly borrowing safety from a gentle new teacher, helped by an honest goodbye, a parent who stays at first and a comfort toy.

passage:
"This is Tanvir," his mother said at the daycare door. "He brought his blanket."

"Hello, Tanvir," said Gurleen, crouching down. "I'm Gurleen. I love your blanket. Shall we sit with Mummy first?"

Tanvir hid his face.

"Can I stay a bit?" his mother asked.

"Please do."

Later, Tanvir handed Gurleen a block.

"Thank you! Shall we build?"

His mother stood up. "Tanvir, Mummy's going to work. I'll be back after nap."

He wailed. Gurleen picked him up. "I've got you. Mummy's coming back after nap."

qa.q: What did Tanvir bring to daycare?
What does Tanvir handing Gurleen a block suggest about his feelings?
qa.a: It suggests he was starting to feel safe and curious with Gurleen after being shy at first.

qa.q: Which choices helped Tanvir trust the new teacher?
qa.a: His mother stayed a while, said an honest goodbye with a clear return time, Gurleen greeted him warmly and held him, and he had his blanket.

qa.q: How does Gurleen see the first morning?
qa.a: Gurleen sees it as something to take slowly, gladly letting his mother stay while Tanvir settles.

grounding: Shows a toddler slowly borrowing safety from a warm new daycare teacher, with a parent who stays at first, an honest goodbye and a comfort item.
